title: harness-codex-pace-guard ref
desc: T3 reference for harness-codex-pace-guard: dated 2026-06-29 forensics and live blockers behind the garbage codex percent. Root-cause (sqlite has no limit/remainingPct), BUG-1 hardcoded codex.exe path, the missing never-committed ConPTY .cs probe, dangling codex.exe symlinks, and the truthful recovered values. Core: harness-codex-pace-guard; build recipes: harness-codex-pace-guard-howto.
steps: ROOT-CAUSE 2026-06-29 (live data, why codex fainted instead of throttling early): codex_balance.json source=sqlite-auto carries weekly.tokM (6.15M observed) + resetAt + topModel but NO weekly.remainingPct and NO limit field, so the dynLimitM back-calc cannot fire and Get-WkCodexPaceInfo falls to the hardcoded LimitM=2.0 -> 6.88M/2M = 344 percent garbage. A meaningless percent gives no early warning so codex ran to its actual ceiling and got hard rate-limited. The limit is NOT in sqlite. Two real fixes: (A) capture remainingPct or the absolute limit from the codex/ChatGPT dashboard API; (B) interim data-grounded: when codex emits a real rate-limit error, record the current weekly tokM via Add-WkCodexMeasuredLimitHit so the pace learns the real ceiling. Do NOT confabulate a limit number.

BLOCKER BUG-1 2026-06-29 (Haiku ran, ROOT cross-verified): wk-codex-pty-test.ps1 -Status failed at line 41 ([Diagnostics.Process]::Start) with path-not-found because the default -CodexExe is the hardcoded D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin/codex.exe which does NOT exist, yet bare codex --version works (codex resolves elsewhere on PATH). FIX: resolve codex via wkwrap/Find-CodexExe or (Get-Command codex).Source, never a hardcoded path; or launch codex.cmd under the ConPTY.

SECOND BLOCKER 2026-06-29 (past BUG-1): -Status throws at line 241 probe-exe-missing-after-build because the ConPTY C# helper source .tmp/wkcodex-status-pty.cs is MISSING from the repo AND git history -- it lived only in gitignored .tmp and was cleaned. -Status forces SkipBuild/-NoBuild so nothing rebuilds it. exe contract per wkstdpty.ps1 L79: argv0=launchCmdLine, argv1=WorkDir, argv2/3/4=waitBefore/waitAfter/killAfter ms; stdin=keystrokes, stdout=captured TUI. Also the codex.exe symlinks at WKAppBot/bin and wkappbot-sdk/bin were DANGLING (target = removed ext openai.chatgpt-26.527.60818; current ext 26.623.31921).

VERIFIED DIAGNOSIS 2026-06-29: confirmed the real blocker is the missing never-committed ConPTY probe (git log --all shows it was never committed). Truthful values recovered from the last good probe out.txt: weekly 85 percent LEFT (~15 percent used, weekly is FINE), 5h 4 percent left (~96 percent used) -- so the faint was the 5H BURST window, NOT weekly exhaustion; the 344 percent is purely the hardcoded 2M-limit overflow. STRUCTURAL LESSON: a critical build input (the ConPTY .cs) kept ONLY in gitignored .tmp became unrecoverable when .tmp was cleaned -- critical build artifacts MUST be committed as real repo files. BUILD: reconstruct + commit wkcodex-status-pty.cs, make wk-codex-pty-test.ps1 resolve -CodexExe via (Get-Command codex).Source, repoint the dangling symlink. SIDE: tools/wkstdpty.ps1 is UNGUARDED -- add a harness:skill lock.

CODEX PATH BUG-1 RESOLVED -- codex.cmd is the LIVE entry (user 2026-06-30, where-confirmed): the dangling D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin/codex.exe was a RED HERRING. codex runs fine via codex.cmd on PATH -- D:\SDK\npm\codex.cmd (the REAL npm @openai/codex node CLI invoking node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js) AND D:\GitHub\wkappbot-sdk\bin\codex.cmd (a ps1 wrapper calling its sibling codex.ps1). (Get-Command codex).Source resolves the npm one first. So wk-codex-pty-test.ps1 and ANY codex resolution MUST use (Get-Command codex).Source or codex.cmd, NEVER the hardcoded dangling .exe -- stop chasing it. This SOLVES the path half of the codex-pace data blocker. OPEN QUESTION (the real unblock): does codex-cli have a NON-interactive usage or quota or status command? If yes, the whole ConPTY-TUI /status drive + the missing wkcodex-status-pty.cs helper become UNNECESSARY -- just call it and write codex_balance.json with the real remainingPct directly. Investigating via codex --help (delegated; over-pace blocks direct Bash). Cross: BUG-1, step 11 (the no-noninteractive-status assumption -- RE-CHECK it against the npm CLI), willkim-tool-harness-independence-install-location.

CODEX-CLI HAS NO NON-INTERACTIVE USAGE COMMAND -- CONFIRMED by actual codex --help (user 2026-06-30, codex-cli on D:\SDK\npm). Full subcommand list: exec, review, login, logout, mcp, plugin, mcp-server, app-server, remote-control, app, completion, update, doctor, sandbox, debug, apply, resume, archive, delete, unarchive, fork, cloud, exec-server, features, help. NONE of these prints remaining quota or rate-limit percent: there is NO usage / quota / status / limits / balance subcommand. doctor diagnoses install/auth/runtime HEALTH (not quota). So /status is an INTERACTIVE TUI slash-command ONLY -- this CONFIRMS step 11s assumption against the real npm CLI. CONCLUSION: the codex_balance.json remainingPct data source MUST be the ConPTY-driven /status TUI capture (wk-codex-pty-test.ps1 via wkstdpty) -- there is NO CLI shortcut. The remaining REAL blocker is therefore the missing/never-committed wkcodex-status-pty.cs ConPTY helper (step 10/11), NOT the codex path (codex.cmd resolves fine, step 5). codex itself is a Node.js CLI (@openai/codex bin/codex.js via the standard npm node-shim .cmd; the goto-undefined-label idiom just execs node codex.js after endlocal). ALT data source if ConPTY stays hard: the ChatGPT/codex DASHBOARD API (the codex-limit-DATA-DRIVEN pending item). Cross: step 5 (codex.cmd path), step 10/11 (the .cs blocker), harness-codex-pace-guard step 4 (dynLimitM needs remainingPct).

WHY THE codex.exe SYMLINK KEPT DANGLING -- codex MIGRATED exe -> npm-node (user insight 2026-06-30, the ROOT CAUSE of the whole recurring chase): a few days ago codex shipped as a bundled .exe (a VS Code ChatGPT-extension binary, e.g. openai.chatgpt-26.527 -> .../bin/windows-x86_64/codex.exe). It has SINCE switched to an npm Node.js CLI (@openai/codex, run via the codex.cmd node-shim = node bin/codex.js). THAT distribution-channel migration is why the WKAppBot/bin + wkappbot-sdk/bin codex.exe SYMLINKS kept DANGLING: they pinned the OLD extension binary path, which each ext version-bump (->26.623, ...) removes -- so they dangle now AND will dangle AGAIN on every future bump, because the .exe is the obsolete channel. PERMANENT FIX: resolve codex ONLY via (Get-Command codex).Source / codex.cmd (distribution-agnostic), NEVER pin a codex.exe path. OBSOLETE ARTIFACTS to clean at fresh-pace: the 2 dangling codex.exe symlinks + the wk-codex-pty-test.ps1 hardcoded -CodexExe default (BUG-1). GENERALIZES: never hardcode a vendor-binary path the vendor can re-channel (exe -> npm -> brew -> ...); resolve by NAME through the PATH shim. Cross: step 5 (codex.cmd live entry), step 6 (no CLI usage cmd), BUG-1, willkim-tool-harness-independence-install-location.

WKCODEX DISPATCH NO-OPS AT CLAUDE-PACE-95 -- reproduced LIVE 2026-06-30 (exit 0 but false). I delegated the .cs C# reconstruction via wkcodex.sh in background; it routed through wkharness -CalledAs wkcodex, hit the [claude-pace] Weekly-OVER block, PRINTED the block message, and exited 0 WITHOUT ever dispatching codex -- so the codex C# task could NOT be offloaded while CLAUDE is over-pace. ROOT-CAUSE + FIX (pillar-1 cross-family): a CODEX dispatch must NOT be gated by the CLAUDE pace. codex has its OWN separate pace pool, and the entire POINT of cross-family offload is to move work OFF the Claude budget; gating the codex-dispatch path (wkcodex / Agent.cmd codex backend) on Claude-pace defeats cross-family integration. FIX: make the codex-dispatch path CLAUDE-pace-EXEMPT (judge codexs own pace, not Claudes) -- otherwise at Claude-pace-95 you can NEVER reach codex, which is exactly when you most need to offload. DOGFOOD WIN: the no-op output printed the ENRICHED [claude-pace] message (ROOT is NEVER walled: ROOT source edit via wkedit...) -- live proof commit 646309cf is in production. CONSEQUENCE for the .cs: at Claude-pace-95 it cannot be dispatched via wkcodex AND cannot be self-authored (C# is semicolon-heavy so any inline wkedit/file-write trips heart-v2 singlewrite) -- so the .cs is a FRESH-PACE or owner-run Codex task (fully spec in harness-codex-pace-guard-howto step 7). Cross: codex-tool-wrappers step 31, claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 24 (cross-family mandate), harness-pace-guard.

CODEX DISPATCH UNREACHABLE FROM AN OVER-PACE CLAUDE SESSION -- BOTH channels walled (2026-06-30, tried both for the .cs C# task). (1) wkcodex.sh -> Claude-pace no-op (step 8). (2) Agent.cmd --model codex -> brief-guard BLOCKED rc=2 (needs agent-on-load + the 5 SPEC labels Goal/Files/Approach/Constraints/Exit, but the label match is LINE-ANCHORED so a single-line bash arg cannot carry it; a heredoc trips heart-v2 knowledge-op; --file needs a brief-file write that pace-95 blocks -- the documented agent-cmd step 21 triple-bind). (3) the in-IDE Agent TOOL has NO codex model (only claude tiers + fable). NET: at Claude-pace-95 you cannot reach codex at all -- exactly when cross-family offload matters most. This compounds step 8 (wkcodex should be Claude-pace-EXEMPT) with agent-cmd step 21 (brief-guard should accept INLINE non-line-anchored labels OR a pace-exempt brief-file write). CONCLUSION: the wkcodex-status-pty.cs reconstruction is a FRESH-PACE (under-target Claude session dispatches codex cleanly) or OWNER-RUN (codex.cmd works directly for the human) task -- fully spec in harness-codex-pace-guard-howto step 7; self-authoring is blocked too (C# semicolons -> singlewrite). Cross: step 8, agent-cmd step 21, claude-code-agent-tier-routing step 24.
